subject: math-aa-sl
title: Parity of a difference of squares
stem: Let n be an integer and let $D=(n+4)^2-n^2$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Prove that D is divisible by $8$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why checking several integer values would not be a proof.

steps.text: $n+2$ is an integer, so D is an integer multiple of $8$.
A finite set of examples cannot establish the claim for every integer; the algebra covers an arbitrary integer.

verification.method: Independent symbolic/numeric and mathematical reasoning checks
verification.notes: Displayed parameters were recalculated; see the per-record AA SL author-review ledger. Identity expanded symbolically; the integer factor, rather than examples, completes the divisibility proof.

subject: math-aa-sl
title: A rational identity with restrictions
stem: Let $x\ne0$ and $x\ne-2$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Prove that $\frac1x-\frac1{x+2}\equiv\frac{2}{x(x+2)}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why the excluded values must remain excluded after simplification.

steps.text: Use common denominator $x(x+2)$ on the left.
The numerator is $2$, giving the required right-hand side for all allowed x.
The original denominators are zero there; an algebraic identity only asserts equality where both sides are defined.

verification.method: Independent symbolic/numeric and mathematical reasoning checks
verification.notes: Displayed parameters were recalculated; see the per-record AA SL author-review ledger. Rational difference checked symbolically; domain restrictions independently reviewed.

title: Comparing nominal and effective interest

parts.prompt: State one assumption of this model.

subject: math-aa-sl
title: Linear versus multiplicative progress
stem: In week n, project A completes $A_n=8+4(n-1)$ units and project B completes $B_n=4(1.25)^{n-1}$ units. These are weekly outputs, not cumulative totals.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the first week in which project B has a greater weekly output than project A.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why the two models should not necessarily be used indefinitely.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find each project’s cumulative output over the first $13$ weeks. Which total is larger?

steps.text: Compare $4(1.25)^{n-1}$ with $8+4(n-1)$ using an integer table or graph.
At week $12$, $B=46.6\leq A=52$; at week $13$, $B=58.2>A=56$. Earlier integer weeks also satisfy $B\leq A$.
Capacity or resource constraints may prevent either constant additive increases or constant percentage growth from continuing.
$S_B=275$ units; project A has the larger cumulative output.

verification.method: Independent symbolic/numeric and mathematical reasoning checks
verification.notes: Displayed parameters were recalculated; see the per-record AA SL author-review ledger. All integer weeks up to first crossing enumerated independently; weekly output is distinguished from sums.
